title: Field Customer Success Specialist (Field Service Engineer), Vending Technology
description:
ABOUT THE JOB

When a customer's own technicians have tried everything and the machine still won't behave, you're the one they call.

Our client makes vending machines and the payment systems that go in them, with manufacturing in the UK. Once a machine is sold, the operator who bought it runs it and maintains it with their own service team. So by the time a problem reaches you, the manual has been followed and the obvious fixes have failed. What's left is the interesting part: a component that has drifted out of tolerance, a software change with a side effect, a third-party payment device that isn't talking to the machine the way it should.

Your job is to find the real cause, not only to get the machine running again. Often you'll solve it remotely, which is how the customer would like it: a machine that's down is losing them revenue, and on some sites they're on the clock with their own customers. Sometimes you'll be on site with them. You own the problem from the first call to the fix. You tell the customer honestly where things stand, bring what you've found back into the business, and work with quality, supply chain, and engineering until there's a solution that holds up in the field.

You make sure nobody has to solve it twice. What you learn becomes a troubleshooting guide, a training session, a short video, or a better workflow in Salesforce, so the next customer gets to the answer faster. The team is working out how AI can help with that, and you'd have a real hand in it.

You'll be part of a team that supports customers across Europe, working alongside sales, engineering, and customer service. Training customers' technicians, support new launches, and feed what you hear in the field back to product design.

THE MANDATE

Our client is not looking for a repair technician who works through the manual and stops there. The customer has already done that. They're not looking for a salesperson either, or for someone who needs to be pointed in a direction before they'll move.

They're seeking someone who can troubleshoot electromechanical equipment and the software that runs it, keep going until they reach the root cause, and stay pragmatic about when a fix is good enough to take back to the field. The right person is steady with a customer who's under pressure and wants an answer now, confident enough to tell them what the best solution really is, and independent enough to set their own direction and sense-check it.

Duties and responsibilities
  • Give customers technical support, remotely and on site, and be the escalation point when their own teams can't resolve an issue
  • Troubleshoot and resolve configuration, installation, and operating problems, including equipment that isn't right out of the box
  • Lead root cause investigations with engineering, quality, operations, and product teams, and see recurring issues through to a lasting fix
  • Manage your cases in Salesforce: track progress, keep accurate records, and spot the patterns in what keeps coming up
  • Deliver certified training and onboarding for customers and their technicians, so they can operate, maintain, and troubleshoot the machines themselves
  • Support new product introductions, evaluations, and customer pilots, from installation planning and commissioning to rollout and early-life support, coordinating customer readiness with the teams involved
  • Write and keep current the user guides, service bulletins, technical procedures, troubleshooting documents, and customer instructions
  • Produce training videos and digital learning content that help customers help themselves
  • Gather customer feedback, pick out the concerns that keep recurring, whether about the product, its quality, how usable it is, or the service, and report them in a structured way to the teams who can act on them
  • Look for better ways to deliver support, including where AI and better tools can help
  • Help retain and grow the key customer accounts in your territory

LOCATION & WORK MODEL

  • Field-based in the UK, working from home between customer visits
  • Regular travel across the UK and Ireland. A call can come from Glasgow as easily as from London.
  • Ideally you live along the M4 corridor west of London or within reach of Manchester, about two hours from one of the company's UK sites, which you'll use for customer training
Experience and qualifications

Essential:

  • A background in technical support, field service, customer success, or a customer-facing engineering role
  • Strong diagnostic and troubleshooting skills across electromechanical equipment and software
  • Experience delivering training and presentations to customers
  • Able to explain technical ideas to technical and non-technical people alike
  • Excellent customer relationship skills, including with customers who are under pressure
  • Clear written communication and good documentation habits
  • Comfortable working independently and managing your own priorities
  • A full driving licence valid in the UK. The role involves regular driving to customer sites across the UK and Ireland in a company vehicle.
  • Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. Proof will be required before employment starts.

Desirable:

  • Experience in payment, kiosk, vending, coffee, beverage, or other electromechanical technology
  • Strong working knowledge of Salesforce
  • Experience making instructional or digital training content, including video
  • An interest in using AI to improve troubleshooting, documentation, and customer support
  • French or German. Spanish is also useful.
